review_notes: I read the whole file and looked for repeated nontrivial proofs. I found two repeated p = 0 / p = ∞ / 0 < p < ∞ case-split patterns. Other repetitions, such as `Memℓp.const_smul` against `norm_const_smul_le`, and the `ite` bookkeeping in the `single` lemmas, are short or differ enough that I did not report them. I checked line numbers and the surrounding declarations with Read. I could not compile any replacement. The `Memℓp.mono'` replacement uses only the existing signature. The norm-invariance lemma is a proposal, and its `ext`/`simp` steps are untested.

findings.problem: `Memℓp.neg` and `Memℓp.star_mem` (lines 790–797) have the same three-way split on `p`. In each case the proof unfolds the finite-support, `BddAbove` and `Summable` formulations and checks that the pointwise norm (and the zero set) is unchanged by `-` or `star`. The only fact used is `‖-f i‖ = ‖f i‖` (resp. `‖star (f i)‖ = ‖f i‖`). The file already has `Memℓp.mono'`, which handles all exponents from a pointwise norm bound. It is stated before `neg`, so using it creates no dependency problem. The two exponent-by-exponent proofs duplicate that machinery.
findings.proposed_change: Replace both proofs with the existing norm-domination lemma. For `Memℓp.neg`: `hf.mono' fun i => by simp`. For `Memℓp.star_mem`: `hf.mono' fun i => by simp`, using `norm_star` (a simp lemma under `NormedStarGroup`). Here `mono'` is instantiated with `F := E`, `g := f`, and `fun i => (norm_neg _).le` or `(norm_star _).le` gives the hypothesis. The `neg_iff` and `star_iff` wrappers are unchanged. Any further map that preserves pointwise norms can be handled the same way.
findings.benefit: This removes about 12 lines of duplicated case analysis. The proofs state the real reason the property is preserved, namely that norms are unchanged pointwise. Future changes to the `Memℓp` definition then need maintenance in only one place (`mono`), not in `neg`, `star_mem` and similar lemmas.

findings.problem: `lp.norm_toNorm` (lines 480–485) proves by cases on `p` that the `lp` norm depends only on the pointwise norms `‖x i‖`. `lp.norm_neg` (lines 533–543) and the `NormedStarGroup (lp E p)` instance (lines 820–827) redo this exponent-by-exponent argument. `norm_neg` also handles the empty-index case and uses `IsLUB.unique` and `HasSum.unique`. The star instance repeats the three-way split on `p`, with an extra impossible `p = 0` case. All three reduce to the fact that `‖x‖` is determined by `fun i => ‖x i‖`, which `norm_toNorm` already encodes.
findings.proposed_change: After `norm_toNorm`, add one lemma, for example `lp.norm_eq_of_norm_apply_eq {F : α → Type*} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (F i)] {x : lp E p} {y : lp F p} (h : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ = ‖y i‖) : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖`. Proof sketch: `toNorm x = toNorm y` by `ext`/`funext` from `h`, since `toNorm` has the coordinate `‖x i‖`. Then `rw [← norm_toNorm (x := x), ← norm_toNorm (x := y), this]`. Rewrite `norm_neg` as `norm_eq_of_norm_apply_eq fun i => by simp`. Rewrite `norm_star_le f` as `le_of_eq (norm_eq_of_norm_apply_eq fun i => by simp)`. This lemma has no `p ≠ 0` hypothesis, so the star instance no longer needs the `exfalso` branch or the `Fact (1 ≤ p)` argument. All of this sits after `norm_toNorm` and uses only `lp.star_apply` and `norm_star`.
findings.benefit: One lemma carries the p-case analysis. `norm_neg` and `norm_star_le` shrink to one-line proofs. The `p = 0`, `p = ∞` and `0 < p < ∞` cases are no longer duplicated, including the empty-index special case. The lemma is also reusable for other norm-preserving maps.
